newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bonds rallied to their strongest levels in over three months on Thursday after a technical break triggered a rush of local and offshore buying.
At the 1400 GMT finish, the key R150 was pegged at a 15.31 percent yield from 15.40 percent on Wednesday.

After a relatively benign morning session, dealers said what appeared to be an offshore order pushed the R150 through technical resistance at 15.36 percent, catching some players short and triggering widespread buying.
"We saw big demand from offshore and local institutions," a dealer said.
As the yield approached the 15.25 percent level -- an option strike level -- dealers said the market could be pulled even lower.
"The lower we go there might be options which have been written and have to be covered in case they are called," one trader said. "It's sort of being sucked down at the moment."
Dealers cited the continued easing of liquidity pressures on the money as the main reason behind strength in the long-end on the day.

Reserve Bank figures showed the shortage fell to 8.49 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.937 billion rand on Tuesday, despite a rise in notes and coins in circulation to 19.948 billion rand from 19.422 billion rand previously.
Short-term rates also continued to ease, with three-month NCD rates quoted at between 16.90 and 16.95 percent offered -- their lowest level since November 9 -- from 17.05 percent on Wednesday.
Chris Doyle, assistant general manager at UAL Merchant Bank Treasury, said the lower shortage was the prime mover behind the fall in short-term rates.
"Primarily it is what you are seeing in the shortage," Doyle said.

"If you look at the forwards, they are saying it is attractive for foreigners to bring money into the country instead of the local banks to place their dollars offshore. So we are starting to see a reversal of flows," he said.
Forward rates continued to fall in line with the easing of money market liquidity pressures. Three-month forward rates are at their lowest levels since mid-October, as are one-year forwards.
The rand took little cognisance of the bullish tone on the gilt market, edging weaker on month-end importer demand as well as speculative offshore dollar demand, dealers said.
It was last quoted at 4.5645/5675 against the dollar from 4.5595/5625 on Wednesday.

"It opened a little weaker on the usual sort of demand," one trader said, referring to players who sell dollars on Wednesday and buy them back on Thursday in order to pick up carry points which amount to about half-a-cent.
"The rand tried to go stronger on the back of the bonds but there were a whole load of bids from importers," the dealer said. "It held pretty steady around the 4.56 area before the offshore hit it."
He said the rand was expected to move sideways on Friday as most players held their long positions ahead of the weekend.
"But it should start to firm again next week...we will probably see 4.53," he added.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 7.3918/4013 against sterling from 7.4032/4103 on Wednesday and at 0.3590/3593 marks from 0.3593/3598 previously.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 99.16 million rands worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 3.41 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative turnover on the bond market on Wednesday was 7.23 billion rand from 6.49 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
